The image shows soybean stems that are distinctly **green** while the pods are fully mature and tan/brown. This contrast — green stem retention with mature pods — is the hallmark symptom of Green Stem Disorder. The pods appear normal in shape (some flat/poorly filled, which is common with this condition), and the stems show no lesions or blight typical of fungal diseases.
